questions.q: Why did the 1977 dietary report avoid telling Americans to eat less meat?
a: The committee chair owned cattle farms
Scientists had proven saturated fat was harmless
Meat producers threatened a lawsuit
The report focused only on sugar and salt
questions.why: Lesson 1 says George McGovern's cattle interests led to the vaguer wording about animal fat.

a: Fat and cholesterol in meat and dairy cause heart disease
Low-fat dairy protects against type 2 diabetes
Animal protein is the main source of vitamins
Calories matter more than the nutrients in food
questions.why: Lesson 1 describes it as the idea that fat and cholesterol cause heart disease, resting on two shaky studies.

questions.q: What happened as Americans followed nutrition science more closely?
a: Obesity rose and diet-related disease did not improve
Heart attack admissions fell sharply across the country
Life expectancy dropped below that of the 1950s
Food labels became shorter and easier to read
questions.why: Lesson 2 says three in four Americans are overweight and better medicine, not better eating, cut heart deaths.

questions.q: What shopping rule does Pollan offer about ingredients?
a: Skip products with more than five ingredients
Buy only items marked as heart healthy
Choose foods with added vitamins and fiber
Prefer packages that list calories per serving
questions.why: Lesson 3 says a long ingredient list means a test result, not food, and names yogurt as the simple ideal.

questions.q: What does the grandma test mean?
a: Do not eat anything your grandmother would not recognize
Cook the same meals your family ate growing up
Buy food only from local farmers markets
Trust old recipes over modern cookbooks
questions.why: Lesson 3 says if your grandmother would not eat it or call it food, leave it on the shelf.
